s: Two colleagues in an open-plan office: a woman in her fifties with light skin and grey-streaked auburn hair claps with a broad grin toward a screen, while beside her a man in his forties with olive skin and dark curls claps more slowly, his smile not reaching his eyes, his gaze dropping to the desk.

A woman in her fifties with deep brown skin and short grey-streaked coils stands on a doorstep facing a neighbour in his thirties, holding out a replacement for something she broke. Her eyebrows are raised together in the middle, her eyes stay on his face, her chin is level and one hand is open toward him.

A man in his sixties with tanned skin and thin white hair stands at the back of a living room during a small gathering, half turned away toward a bookshelf with a glass in one hand while another guest talks further off. His chin is tucked into his collar, his gaze slides down to the floor, his shoulders round forward and his free hand presses flat against his chest.

A man in his twenties with medium brown skin and dark wavy hair sits alone on a sofa at night, his phone face-down on the cushion beside him, caught by an old memory. His eyes are squeezed shut, his nose wrinkles in a grimace, one hand covers his mouth and his knees are pulled up toward his chest.

The same woman in her thirties with fair skin and long dark wavy hair now sits at a kitchen table writing a few lines in a small notebook, a mug beside her. Her shoulders sit low and well below her ears, her jaw is loose, her lips are slightly parted and her eyes rest calmly on the page.

A woman in her thirties with medium brown skin and long dark hair closes a bedroom door with deliberate slowness, her fingers on the handle to keep it silent, framed close on her head, shoulders and hand. Her jaw is locked, her eyes are lowered and hard, her lips are pressed shut with the nostrils pinched and her free arm hangs stiff against her side.

A woman in her forties with pale skin and dark hair twisted up puts plates away in a kitchen cupboard with movements that are far too slow and too precise, one plate held in both hands. The muscle at the corner of her jaw stands out, her lips are closed in a straight line, her eyes stay down on the sink and her shoulders are squared and very still.

A man in his fifties with pale skin and a short grey beard makes a dry remark across a Sunday lunch table, his fork paused in the air. One corner of his mouth lifts, his eyebrows are raised in mock innocence, his eyes stay hard and fixed on the young woman opposite, who stops chewing and looks down at her plate.

A man in his twenties with fair skin and short blond hair stands in a hallway holding a single shopping bag, having forgotten what he was asked to buy. His eyebrows are raised in exaggerated blankness, one shoulder shrugs, his mouth is a flat neutral line and his eyes avoid the person in the room.

A man in his forties with deep brown skin and short-cropped hair sits on a bus seat at the end of the day, a bag on his lap and his head resting against the window. His eyelids are heavy, his eyebrows are slack, his mouth hangs slightly open and his hands rest lifelessly on the bag.

A woman in her thirties with medium brown skin and long dark hair sits at a dinner table opposite her partner, a man in his forties with fair skin and a short beard who has just said something careless. Her fork stops halfway up, her lips press into a thin line, her eyebrows flatten and lower, her eyes drop to her plate and her free hand closes slowly on the napkin.

The same woman in her thirties with medium brown skin and long dark hair stands in a living room at night, pointing down at a single sock left on the floor. Her eyebrows are pulled sharply down, her mouth is open mid-sentence, the tendons in her neck stand out and her raised hand is stiff and trembling.

A man in his sixties with fair skin, a short grey beard and glasses sits in a meeting room as a decision is announced without him, his hands folded on the table. His jaw shifts to one side, his eyebrows are low and level, his gaze stays fixed on a point on the table and his folded hands press hard against each other.

A young woman in her twenties with fair skin and shoulder-length brown hair sits at a desk with a very simple form open on her laptop, her hand on the mouse but not moving, framed close on her head and shoulders. Her eyes drift away from the screen toward the window, her mouth pulls to one side, her shoulders sag and her other hand props up her chin.

A man in his twenties with fair skin and messy light brown hair stands in a hallway with his coat on, patting his pockets and checking his keys for the third time. His eyebrows lift high, his eyes are wide and moving, his lips are parted and his free hand already reaches back toward the door handle.

A woman in her fifties with fair skin and blonde-grey hair sits on a train seat filling a paper diary with colour-coded blocks, her phone on her knee showing another list. Her eyebrows are pulled together in focused tension, her lips move slightly as she counts, her back is rigid and her pen presses hard into the page.

A woman in her forties with pale skin and short red hair turns sharply toward her partner in a kitchen over a small thing, a cupboard door half open in her hand. Her eyebrows snap down, her mouth is open mid-word and her neck is tight; the other person, a man with dark skin and short curls, freezes with a plate in his hands and his eyes widen.

A man in his sixties with light brown skin and short grey hair comes back into a kitchen to check the oven dials again, one hand on the counter. His eyes are narrowed and scanning, his eyebrows are low, his mouth is slightly open and his free hand hovers just above the dial.

A young woman in her twenties with pale skin and long straight black hair sits on the edge of her sofa at night, her thumb hovering over a phone as she cancels plans. The inner ends of her eyebrows are raised, her mouth pulls to one side, her shoulders are lifted and her other arm wraps across her stomach.

A man in his forties with olive skin and short dark hair lies awake on his back in bed at night, the duvet up to his chest, eyes open on the ceiling. His eyebrows are slightly raised and pinched together, his lips are pressed, one hand rests on his sternum and the other grips the edge of the duvet.

The same man in his forties with olive skin and short dark hair sits at a kitchen table in daylight, drawing a line down the middle of a notebook page to sort what kept him awake, a cup of tea beside him. His forehead is smooth, his eyes are lowered to the page in mild concentration, his mouth is relaxed and his shoulders sit low and well below his ears.

A young man with brown skin and short twisted locs leans halfway into the office of a manager, one hand on the door frame, framed close on his head and shoulders. His shoulders are pulled up toward his ears, his head tilts apologetically, his eyebrows are raised together in the middle and his mouth makes a small hesitant smile.

A man in his fifties with pale skin and short grey hair takes a heavy shopping bag out of the hands of a younger relative in a hallway, already turning toward the kitchen with it. The inner ends of his eyebrows lift, his smile is quick and thin, his eyes avoid the other person and his shoulders are set in a resigned line.

A man in his thirties with brown skin and a trimmed beard sits at an open-plan desk, agreeing to take on a task handed to him late in the day. He nods with a tight, quick smile, his eyebrows lift and pinch in the middle, his eyes drop to the paper he has been given and his other hand grips the arm of his chair.

A woman in her twenties with pale skin and a short dark bob quietly gathers a stack of dishes from a shared kitchen counter to wash them herself. Her lips are pressed together, her eyes stay on the sink, her eyebrows are slightly drawn and her shoulders are set in a resigned line.

A young man with brown skin and short twisted locs stands beside a colleague’s desk in an open-plan office, about to ask a question he has every right to ask. His shoulders are pulled up toward his ears, his head tips to one side, his eyebrows are raised together in the middle and one hand half-covers the other in front of his chest.

A man in his forties with olive skin and thick dark hair sits at a family table, one hand slightly raised as he takes the blame to end an argument. His eyebrows are pulled up in the middle, his gaze is lowered to the tablecloth, his mouth is tight and his shoulders round inward, while a relative opposite him sits back with folded arms.

A woman in her sixties with deep brown skin and grey locs sits in an armchair with a closed book on her lap, going over a decision again. Her eyes are unfocused and turned slightly down, her eyebrows knit in the centre, one hand covers the other tightly in her lap and her jaw is set.

A man in his sixties with deep brown skin and close-cropped white hair sits alone at a kitchen table in the middle of the night with a glass of water, replaying a conversation. His eyes are fixed on the middle distance, his eyebrows are drawn up in the centre, one hand rubs slowly across his mouth and his shoulders are heavy and low.

The woman in her twenties with pale skin and short bleached hair now sits on a bench beside her friend in her fifties with light brown skin and grey-streaked hair, turned toward her with her hands resting still on her knees. Her eyebrows are level and her gaze is steady and open on the face of her friend, while the shoulders of the older woman have dropped and her mouth softens at one corner.

A man in his thirties with light brown skin and short black hair sits in a car stuck in traffic, hands low on the steering wheel, framed close on his head and shoulders. The muscle at the corner of his jaw stands out, his lips are closed and pressed thin, his eyes stare straight ahead and his shoulders are pulled up toward his ears.

A woman in her twenties with fair freckled skin and long red wavy hair sits on the top step of a staircase, one forearm pressed across her stomach. Her eyebrows are drawn together, her eyes are lowered and unfocused, her shoulders are lifted and her collarbones stand out with the ribcage held high, and her other hand holds a phone loosely.

A woman in her forties with fair skin and dark hair in a ponytail sits in a meeting listening to a decision she disagrees with, a pen still in her hand. The muscles at the hinge of her jaw stand out, her lips are closed in a straight line, her gaze is level and unmoving and her free hand curls into a loose fist on the table.

A young man in his twenties with medium brown skin and short curly hair stands in a queue at a bakery, one hand pressed flat against his stomach under his open jacket. His eyebrows are drawn together, his eyes move around without settling, his shoulders are lifted with the ribcage held high and his other hand fiddles with his phone.

A woman in her thirties with pale skin and long light brown hair stands in a hallway just after a phone call, one hand at the base of her throat. Her chin dimples, she swallows hard, the inner ends of her eyebrows lift high and her lips are parted as if a sentence stopped halfway.

A man in his fifties with deep brown skin and short grey hair sits at a desk in an open-plan office, screen light on his face, his shoulders lifted almost to his ears without him noticing. His brow is furrowed, his eyes are narrowed in concentration, his neck has disappeared into his collar and both hands hover over the keyboard.

A woman in her forties with light olive skin and dark wavy hair lies on her side in bed in the small hours, eyes wide open in the dark. Her eyebrows are slightly raised and tense, her mouth is closed and still, one hand is tucked under her cheek and her whole body is curled and rigid.

A woman in her forties with deep brown skin and braided hair pulled back sits on a chair in a waiting room, a folder on her knees, minutes before an interview. Her eyes flick toward a closed door, her eyebrows are slightly raised, she chews the inside of her cheek and one hand is pressed flat on her stomach.

A man in his thirties with pale skin and short sandy hair sits at the end of a sofa on a Sunday evening, a cold cup of tea in front of him, looking at an empty armchair. His gaze is still and heavy, the inner ends of his eyebrows lift, his mouth turns down slightly at the corners and one hand rests on his stomach.

A man in his forties with pale skin and a short dark beard stands alone in a stairwell just outside a meeting room, one hand flat against the wall, taking ten seconds for himself. His jaw has come unclenched and his lips are slightly parted, his shoulders sit low and well below his ears, his eyelids are half closed and his forehead is smooth.

A woman in her thirties with warm olive skin and dark wavy shoulder-length hair and a man in his thirties with light skin and chestnut curls sit across a small kitchen table at night, one mug between them. Both lean forward and speak at the same moment: nostrils flared and lips pressed thin between sentences, brows low and drawn together, one hand raised palm-up in protest while the other grips the edge of the table, chins pushed forward, eyes locked.

A man in his forties with deep brown skin and short curly hair stands by a window, arms crossed tight against his chest, chin tucked toward his collar, gaze sliding away on a diagonal from the person speaking to him, the corner of his mouth pulled down on one side, one shoulder already turned toward the door.

A woman in her fifties with pale freckled skin and auburn wavy hair raises one open palm in a calm, gentle stop gesture, jaw visibly loosening, eyelids lowered, her other hand resting flat on her own chest as she breathes out slowly, shoulders settling down away from her neck.

A man in his thirties with brown skin and short curly hair stands at a kitchen sink holding a wet plate, shoulders sagging, head turned back over his shoulder toward someone off-frame, mouth opening as if to speak and then closing again, the corners of his mouth pulled down and his chin faintly creased, tired eyes with a faint shine.

A man in his sixties with light tan skin, a grey beard and wavy grey hair sits alone at a café table with two cups, one untouched. He glances at his watch, lips pressed into a thin line and nostrils slightly flared, his other hand tapping the tabletop, eyes flicking toward the door with the lower lids tight, one eyebrow riding higher than the other.

Two people at a dinner table seen from the side: a woman in her thirties with dark skin and braided hair looks down at a phone that lights her face from below, absorbed, lips slightly parted; across from her a man in his thirties with East Asian features holds his fork motionless above his plate, eyes fixed on her, the corners of his mouth drawn down, blinking slowly, his free hand flat on the tablecloth.

A woman in her seventies with pale skin and short white hair and a man in his forties with olive skin sit at opposite ends of a small table after a meal, neither speaking: she turns the ring on her finger round and round, gaze fixed on the tablecloth, lips rolled inward; he looks at the wall just past her shoulder, jaw set, swallowing once, one hand flat beside an untouched cup.

A woman in her forties with medium brown skin and dark wavy hair sits on a sofa mid-argument, body angled forward, one hand chopping the air, mouth open on a fast sentence, chin pushed forward and nostrils flared; at the other end of the sofa a man in his forties with pale skin and chestnut hair sits with closed fists on his knees, eyes locked on the floor, jaw clenched, one knee bouncing, his lips moving silently as if rehearsing his reply.

A woman in her thirties with light brown skin and dark hair pulled back sits alone on the edge of a bed in lamplight, listening toward the next room, her whole body still: lower eyelids tight, eyes wide and unmoving, breath held, one hand closed around the other in her lap, head slightly retracted between her shoulders.

A man in his twenties with deep brown skin and short twists stands in a doorway with one open hand raised softly, eyes meeting the other person’s, eyebrows level, mouth shaped on a calm short sentence, breathing out through slightly parted lips; a woman in her twenties with light skin and red wavy hair looks up at him from the sofa, eyebrows raised high and mouth just opening, caught mid-surprise.

A woman in her thirties with tan skin and curly dark hair walks alone outdoors in evening light, hands deep in her coat pockets, breathing out a visible cloud, the crease between her eyebrows smoothing out, cheeks still flushed, gaze lifted toward the end of the street.

Two people sitting side by side on a couch, turned toward each other: a woman in her fifties with dark brown skin and short grey natural hair listens with her head tilted, chin resting on her hand, blinking slowly, lips still; a man in his fifties with olive skin and salt-and-pepper hair speaks slowly with one open hand in front of him, eyebrows lifted at their outer ends, mouth softening at the end of his sentence.

A man in his thirties with light brown skin and dark wavy hair sits on a sofa in fading daylight, thumb tilting his phone to check the time, the other hand rubbing the back of his neck, mouth pulled down at one corner, shoulders drawn up toward his ears.

A woman in her twenties with pale skin and long chestnut waves glances sideways at a wall clock, lips parted on a small silent sigh, one hand pressed flat over her stomach, the other arm hugging her own waist, the inner ends of her eyebrows tightening.

A man in his sixties with deep brown skin and close-cropped grey hair stands at a kitchen window in the last light of the afternoon, a dish towel forgotten over one shoulder, arms folded, gaze fixed far past the glass, lower eyelids tense, lips pressed together.

A man in his fifties with tan skin and thinning grey hair sits on the very edge of a sofa in warm late-afternoon light, elbows on his knees, fingers laced so tightly the knuckles pale, eyes fixed on one point of the floor, upper eyelids raised, one corner of his mouth twitching, a cup of tea going cold and untouched beside him.

A woman in her twenties with brown skin and box braids sits on a kitchen stool in soft pyjamas, phone held low in one hand, thumb frozen mid-scroll, eyes narrowed at the screen, the muscles around her mouth tightening, her other hand stalled around a mug she has forgotten to drink.

A man in his forties with light skin, a red beard and short hair grabs his coat while half-turned away from a cluttered desk, his body already pointed at the door but his eyes pulled back toward the papers, upper lip tense, one hand hovering in mid-air as if he has forgotten something.

A woman in her sixties with olive skin and silver wavy hair lies awake on her side in dim light, eyes wide and fixed on the ceiling, blinking rarely, one hand curled near her chin, her lips moving faintly as if finishing a sentence with someone who is not there, the other hand gripping the edge of the blanket.

A woman in her thirties with deep brown skin and short coiled hair sits on the edge of her bed in lamplight, one finger setting an alarm clock on the nightstand, looking at it sideways, the corner of her mouth pulled down, her free hand resting on the duvet, her body already turned away toward the pillow.

A man in his thirties with East Asian features and straight dark hair sits sideways on a sofa in the blue light of a screen, one knee jiggling, thumb turning the remote over and over without pressing it, eyes flicking away from the screen toward the dark window, eyebrows faintly drawn together, mouth tense — physically there, attention already somewhere else.

A woman in her forties with deep brown skin and short curly hair closes a laptop with both hands and lets out a long breath, eyelids lowered, jaw unclenched, the corners of her mouth lifting slightly, shoulders settling down and back, a closed blank notebook beside her.

A woman in her twenties with light olive skin and dark wavy hair lies on a bed holding a phone above her face in the dark, the screen glow on her features, eyes wide and unblinking with the lower lids tight, her teeth pressing into her lower lip, her other hand curled against her collarbone, knees drawn up.

A man in his thirties with brown skin and a short fade sits on a bus seat staring at his phone, thumb hovering without moving, the crease between his brows deepening, one cheek pulled in as he chews the inside of it, his other hand gripping the strap of his bag.

A woman in her forties with pale skin and auburn hair pinned up stands in a hallway with a small child on her hip and a phone wedged between shoulder and ear, cheeks flushed, chin tucked to hold the phone, laughing mid-sentence with her eyes crinkled, her free hand reaching for something past the edge of the frame.

A young man in his twenties with tan skin and messy dark curls paces an empty living room at night, one hand gripping the back of his neck, the other clenched at his side, eyes fixed on the floor, jaw tight, chin tucked down, his steps short and quick.

A woman in her fifties with deep brown skin and short grey curls stands in an office lift holding a phone in one hand and a stack of folders in the other, giving the screen a distracted half-nod, eyelids relaxed, mouth easy, her attention already moving toward the opening doors.

A man in his sixties with light skin, glasses and short white hair sits at a kitchen table with both hands flat on the wood, looking down at his own hands, the lines across his forehead deepening, lips rolled inward, his shoulders heavy and completely still, a cold cup at the far edge of the table.

A woman in her thirties with East Asian features and straight black hair sits cross-legged on a sofa, phone held in both hands, thumbs poised above the screen, eyes retracing the same lines again, the outer ends of her eyebrows drawing down, her thumb rubbing the edge of the phone case, one heel bouncing fast, a cold mug forgotten beside her.

A man in his forties with brown skin and a trimmed beard walks outdoors in daylight, phone already back in his pocket, chin lifted, shoulders released, a small resolved smile, eyes clear and looking forward.

A woman in her thirties with brown skin and short curly hair sits on the edge of her bed just after the alarm, one hand pressed flat over her stomach, the other braced on the mattress, head hanging forward, eyes not yet fully open, the corners of her mouth pulled down, her whole trunk curved over the hand on her belly.

A man in his twenties with pale skin and dark hair stands in a commuter train holding the overhead bar, gaze fixed on nothing, jaw clenched hard enough to show the muscle at his temple, chest high with shallow quick breathing, his other hand pressed against his coat over his belly.

A woman in her fifties with light tan skin and greying hair in a low bun sits at an open-plan desk, hand hovering over the mouse without clicking, the screen turned away from view, her lower eyelids tight and her gaze unmoving, her upper lip drawn back slightly, her other hand resting on a closed blank notebook.

A man in his forties with deep brown skin and short curly hair stands just outside a meeting room holding blank papers against his chest, nostrils widening on one deliberate deep breath, eyes focused straight ahead, a quick ready half-smile, his weight on the balls of his feet.

A woman in her thirties with olive skin and long dark hair sits in a parked car before work, head tipped back against the headrest, eyes closed, the vertical crease between her brows deep, lips parted on a long slow exhale, both hands still gripping the top of the steering wheel.

A man in his sixties with light skin and white hair carries a tall stack of blank folders with both arms, chin pushed up to hold the top one steady, eyes stretched wide, lips clamped shut, elbows locked, his back curving under the load.

A woman in her twenties with brown skin and curly hair sits at a desk, hands frozen above the keyboard, head turning between two screens and a phone lighting up at the same moment; her gaze darts from one to the next, lower eyelids tight, mouth half open, shoulders sinking — overwhelmed by the room rather than by anyone in it.

A man in his thirties with East Asian features and straight dark hair stands alone in an empty corridor just after a meeting, folders under one arm, holding a polite smile that does not reach his eyes, jaw tight, gaze dropping to the floor, his other arm hanging loose.

A woman in her forties with dark skin and locs stands with one shoulder visibly lower than the other as if carrying an invisible weight on one side, head tilted toward the low side, her mouth pulled into a wry sideways line, one hand rubbing the heavy shoulder.

Two colleagues stand by a coffee machine: a woman in her thirties with pale freckled skin speaks quietly with her eyes lowered and a small relieved smile; a man in his fifties with brown skin listens with a slight nod, his eyebrows lifting in recognition, one hand resting on the machine.

A young man in his twenties with light skin and short blond hair sits upright across a small table from a woman in her forties with deep brown skin, speaking steadily with one open hand gesture, his gaze direct and his jaw relaxed; she leans slightly forward, her head tilted, eyes attentive.

A woman in her sixties with olive skin, glasses and grey hair in a bun sits in a consulting room listening to someone off-frame, pen resting on the desk, head tilted, her eyes warm and steady, the outer corners of her eyes crinkling faintly, one hand open on the desk in a welcoming gesture.

A man in his thirties with light brown skin and dark wavy hair sits on one side of an unmade bed at dawn, the other side untouched, one hand resting flat on the empty sheet, head bowed, eyes red-rimmed and unfocused, his lower lip loose, his breathing shallow and slow.

A woman in her twenties with deep brown skin and long braids reaches automatically for her phone on a kitchen counter and stops, hand hovering in the air as she remembers, her chin puckering, the corners of her mouth pulling down, her eyes filling without spilling.

A woman in her forties with pale skin and short auburn hair sits on a park bench beside a friend, a laugh just fading from her face: eyes still crinkled, mouth still open, but one hand landing over her lips and her eyebrows pulling together as if she has caught herself; the friend, a man in his forties with tan skin, keeps smiling warmly at her.

A man in his fifties with tan skin and greying curls sits at a small two-seat table with the chair opposite him empty, both hands wrapped around a mug he is not drinking, eyes fixed on that empty chair, the corners of his mouth pulled down, his throat swallowing once.

A woman in her thirties with East Asian features and shoulder-length black hair sits holding a folded blank map in her lap, her gaze going through it without seeing, her chin trembling faintly, her thumb stroking the same fold over and over.

A man in his twenties with brown skin and short curls stands in a kitchen having automatically taken two mugs from the shelf, freezing as he notices the second one, his mouth opening slightly, one hard blink, his raised hand staying in mid-air, his jaw going loose.

A woman in her thirties with olive skin and dark curly hair lies curled on a sofa under a blanket at night, phone close to her face, thumb scrolling backwards without stopping, her eyes swollen, her breath catching in her chest, knees drawn up, the crease between her brows deep.

Two friends walk outdoors in bright soft light: a man in his forties with deep brown skin and a shaved head laughs with his head tipped slightly back and his eyes crinkled, and beside him a woman in her forties with pale skin and red hair smiles wide with one hand on his arm, both of them walking loose and open.

A woman in her twenties with brown skin and a high ponytail holds her phone in both hands and presses one deliberate button, chin lifted, jaw set with quiet resolve, her eyes steady though still red, her shoulders squared.

A man in his sixties with light skin and short white hair walks outdoors in cool morning light wearing a coat, hands in his pockets, gaze lifted toward the horizon, his breath faintly visible, his face tired but his step even and steady.

A woman in her fifties with deep brown skin and short grey natural hair writes at a kitchen table under a lamp, pen pressed to a completely blank page, her brows drawn together in concentration, her lips slightly parted, one tear on her cheek, her free hand steadying the paper.

Two people in their thirties sitting at a small kitchen table late in the evening, two mugs and a bowl between them, caught mid-argument, both talking at once. The woman on the left has warm brown skin and long curly hair: her eyebrows are pulled low and together, her mouth open mid-sentence, both hands flat and tense on the table, her chin pushed forward. The man on the right has olive skin and short dark wavy hair: his jaw is clenched, one hand raised palm out at chest height, his shoulders lifted toward his ears, his gaze locked on hers.

A woman in her forties with pale freckled skin and auburn wavy hair stands alone on a stairwell landing, coat still on, one hand on the metal railing. Her eyes are closed, her mouth slightly open on a long exhale, her eyebrows releasing their knot, her shoulders visibly dropping away from her ears, her other hand hanging loose and open at her side.

A man in his twenties with deep brown skin and short twists stands alone in a narrow hallway, facing a closed door suggested in a few lines, a coat left hanging on a hook beside him. His arms hang at his sides with his hands half-open, his eyebrows are raised and pulled together in the middle, his eyes are wide and fixed on the door handle, his lips are parted, his weight tipped forward onto his front foot as if waiting for a sound.

Close-up from the waist up of a young man in his twenties with East Asian features and straight dark hair, sitting at a dinner table. His jaw muscles are visibly tight, his lips pressed thin, his eyebrows lowered and drawn together, his nostrils slightly flared, one hand curled into a loose fist beside a plate, the other gripping the edge of the table, his shoulders lifted and rigid.

A woman in her fifties with deep brown skin and silver-streaked curly hair sits at a kitchen table, speaking to someone just out of frame. She holds one palm up at chest height in a gentle, non-defensive gesture, her other hand flat on the table. Her eyebrows are level, her gaze steady and warm, her mouth calm mid-sentence, her shoulders lowered and squared.

A man in his thirties with light brown skin and short curly hair walks alone on a city sidewalk in a buttoned wool coat, hands in his pockets, a bare tree suggested behind him in a few lines. His breath shows faintly in the cold air, his eyebrows are unknotting, his gaze rests on the ground a few steps ahead, his shoulders sit noticeably lower than his collar, his stride even and unhurried.

Two people meeting again at the same kitchen table. A woman in her sixties with pale skin and short wavy grey hair sits with both hands open on the table, her eyebrows raised slightly in hopeful attention. A man in his thirties with brown skin and dark curly hair lowers himself onto the chair opposite, one hand extended halfway across the table toward hers, his mouth in a small uncertain smile, his shoulders relaxed.

The same living room and the same two people. The woman in her forties with pale freckled skin and auburn hair pinned up stands in the doorway turned back toward the sofa, one hand resting flat on the frame, her shoulders lowered, her eyebrows level, her mouth speaking one short sentence. The man in his forties with medium brown skin and short greying hair looks up at her from the sofa, his eyebrows softening, his hands settling on his knees, the beginning of a small relieved nod in his chin.

A young woman with medium brown skin and dark curly hair sits alone on the edge of a sofa in a living room, facing a closed door suggested in a few lines. Her arms are wrapped around her own ribs, her eyebrows are raised and pulled together in the middle, her eyes are wide and fixed on the door, her lips are parted, her whole body leaning slightly forward as if waiting for a sound.

A man in his forties with light olive skin and wavy chestnut hair sits alone at a kitchen table, a phone face down beside a glass of water. His hands rest loosely one on top of the other, his eyebrows are relaxed, his gaze rests on the middle distance without tension, his back against the chair, his mouth neutral and patient.

A young man in his twenties with pale skin and messy chestnut curls sits down at a small café table across from a friend, arriving late, jacket half off one shoulder. His shoulders are pulled up and inward, his eyebrows lifted in the middle in apology, his mouth in a strained apologetic smile, both hands tucked close to his chest in a small helpless gesture.

A woman in her sixties with deep brown skin and short silver curls sits in an armchair, receiving heartfelt thanks from someone out of frame. Her eyebrows lift, her eyes widen slightly and crinkle at the corners, a surprised genuine smile spreads across her face, one hand rising to rest flat on her collarbone, her shoulders settling back.

Two colleagues beside a desk in an open-plan office, a laptop and a small plant suggested behind them. A woman in her thirties with South Asian features and a long dark braid turns toward her colleague with an open palm gesture and a warm direct smile, eyes bright and steady. A man in his forties with fair skin and short blond hair looks up from his chair, eyebrows raised in pleased surprise, a small shy smile forming.

Two people standing in a kitchen doorway. A woman in her thirties with light tan skin and a dark ponytail apologises yet again: her shoulders are drawn up toward her ears, her eyebrows tented in the middle, both hands making small flustered gestures near her chest, her mouth in a tight apologetic smile. Facing her, a man in his sixties with deep brown skin and short white hair does the reassuring: his eyebrows raised, one palm lifted in a calming gesture, his mouth open on a patient answer, a trace of tiredness at the corners of his eyes.

The same café table and the same two people a moment later. The young man with pale skin and chestnut curls now sits upright, both hands open and relaxed on the table, eyebrows level, eyes meeting hers, a sincere warm smile. The woman with brown skin and short coiled hair softens visibly: her eyebrows lift, her shoulders drop, she leans in with a returning smile, still holding her cup.

A woman in her thirties with medium brown skin and dark wavy hair pauses in an open office doorway, a notebook held against her chest, about to ask a question. Her eyebrows are raised in the middle, her teeth lightly catch her lower lip, her weight is on her back foot, her free hand half-raised in a tiny hesitant knocking gesture.

A man in his forties with deep brown skin and short curly hair sits on the corner of a sofa at night, phone held in both hands, having just sent a very long message.
